title: IReactor.executeBatch runs dependency-ordered multi-document jobs in one call
content:
`executeBatch` takes a set of jobs with declared dependencies and lets the reactor work out the schedule. Each job is `{ key, documentId, actions, dependsOn }`, where `dependsOn` names other jobs by `key`:

```ts
await reactor.executeBatch({
  jobs: [
    { key: "budget",  documentId: budgetId,  actions: [initBudget],  dependsOn: [] },
    { key: "scope",   documentId: scopeId,   actions: [initScope],   dependsOn: [] },
    { key: "project", documentId: projectId, actions: [initProject], dependsOn: ["budget", "scope"] },
    { key: "drive",   documentId: driveId,   actions: [addFiles],    dependsOn: ["project"] },
  ],
});
```

`budget` and `scope` run in parallel; `project` waits for both; `drive` waits for `project`. One call, one result. The reactor handles ordering, parallelism, and failure propagation.

The `batch-progress` recipe frames it against the alternative — four sequential `await`s with manual error handling, no atomicity, and, in the recipe's own comment, "hope nothing interleaves". The value is not saving keystrokes; it is that the dependency graph is *declared* rather than encoded in statement order, so the reactor can parallelise independent work and propagate a failure to exactly the dependents that needed it.

Observability comes from the EventBus rather than the return value. The recipe subscribes to `JOB_PENDING`, `JOB_RUNNING`, `JOB_WRITE_READY`, `JOB_READ_READY` and `JOB_FAILED` to drive a live multi-bar progress display — which is the right shape for a batch, since the per-job statuses arrive at different times and a single awaited promise flattens that away.

Note this is on `IReactor`, the low-level fire-and-forget interface, not on the Promise-based `IReactorClient` wrapper. The recipe's demo runs it against an embedded in-memory reactor (PGlite, no external DB).

Provenance: academy `05-Lookup/00-Cookbook.md`, Batch Progress recipe, academy 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: Each job carries a key, documentId, actions and dependsOn; the reactor resolves ordering, parallelism and failure propagation across documents so callers stop hand-sequencing writes.
